title: Mobile-first design
learningObjectives: Explain mobile-first design and apply responsive design principles.

understand.concept: Mobile-first design begins with a simple layout suitable for narrow viewports, then adds enhancements as more space becomes available. It often uses min-width media queries to progressively introduce columns, navigation arrangements, and richer spacing.
understand.whyItMatters: Starting with constrained space encourages prioritisation and helps avoid treating mobile as a reduced desktop version. It also makes the base stylesheet a useful fallback when media queries are unsupported.
understand.analogy: Build the small, essential arrangement first, then add extra rooms when the available space grows.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; responsive behaviour is determined by CSS layout and viewport/container conditions.

explain.narrative: The base is a single column; a wider viewport adds three columns.

examples.explanation: The base is a single column; a wider viewport adds three columns.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the responsive behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a mobile-first navigation and card layout. Start with one column and add enhancements at a min-width breakpoint.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive page section and test it at narrow, medium, and wide viewport sizes, including longer labels.
hints: Use the browser responsive viewport tools.
Check horizontal overflow and text scaling.
Keep keyboard access and semantic structure intact.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Mobile-first design</title></head><body>
<main class='cards'><article>Learn HTML</article><article>Learn CSS</article><article>Learn JavaScript</article></main><style>.cards{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:1rem;padding:1rem}.cards article{padding:1.2rem;background:#dcefe4}@media(min-width:44rem){.cards{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr))}}</style>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What is the usual starting layout in a mobile-first approach?
questions.explanation: Mobile-first starts with the constrained layout and progressively enhances it.

questions.prompt: What should be included in responsive testing?
options: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.answer: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.explanation: Responsive defects often appear at intermediate widths or with expanded content.
